craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta of landing — rest, fulfillment, no-other-standing; autonomy dawning mid-proof. FIRST LANDING (rasa: śama lands here): rest in own form — fulfillment as rest, not climax. Done-ness (kṛtārthatā) enacted in falling cadence. Rejected: (a) heightening fulfillment → killed: rest here is anti-climax by doctrine. (b) unpacking I-am-this → killed: the formula is the seal, verbatim. Read aloud: CUT-off, THIS-this-GRASP-ing FINDS-ful-FILL-ment-THUS … IS-this it-SELF.

lines: Cut off, this 'this'-grasping finds fulfillment thus:
rest in own form — that grasp, 'I am this,' is this itself.
l4.sanskrit_cite: idam ity asya vicchinnavimarśasya kṛtārthatā yā svasvarūpe viśrāntir vimarśaḥ so 'ham ity ayam

reads_against.argmap: Where does cut-off 'this'-grasping complete? → Severed grasping completes in self-rest — 'I am this,' the done-ness that quickens even the inert.
c1_essence: What never stood cannot stand another: consciousness fits itself to this and I, orders inert selves by double certainty, and completes severed grasping in self-rest (vv10-15).
The same self twofold — breath-bound atom, unbroken whole — gathers in one continuous end-ground where nothing shows more inert than shining (vv16-18).
